stories.title: US interest rates raised for first time in three years
stories.body: Rates were hiked in a unanimous decision despite fierce opposition from President Donald Trump, who had called for a cut.

stories.title: Photos show widespread damage at US sites from Iranian attacks
stories.body: A wrecked air force plane and destroyed buildings are among the images obtained by the BBC's partner CBS News.

stories.title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'
stories.body: Canada is seeking closer ties with EU after a breakdown in relations with the US and its president Donald Trump.

stories.title: Eight children among 21 killed after war-damaged Gaza building collapses, rescuers say
stories.body: Some 10 families had reportedly been living in the six-storey building in Gaza City that was hit by an Israeli strike last year.

stories.title: US House votes to hold billionaire Epstein associate Leon Black in contempt
stories.body: Black - who had business ties to Epstein - declined to appear and provide documents related to the convicted sex offender.

stories.title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms
stories.body: Sam Altman and other tech CEOs say there are incentives to limit advancements in AI, as fears grow over the threats it poses to humanity.

stories.title: Eight German state premiers back Merz amid speculation over future
stories.body: Christian Democratic Union leadership throws its weight behind the chancellor ahead of two state elections this weekend.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says it shot down Houthi drone south of Mecca
stories.body: The Houthis deny targeting the Islamic holy city after the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen accuses them of a "disgraceful act".

stories.title: Trump chief of staff Susie Wiles announces she's cancer-free
stories.body: The 69-year-old White House chief of staff is a powerful figure and particularly close to the US president.

stories.title: Michelin-starred Seoul restaurant fined for using ants as garnish
stories.body: The owner of the acclaimed establishment avoids jail but is made to pay 15 million won (£8,144; $10,965).

stories.title: Charlie Kirk's family alleges 'stunning failures' by Utah officials led to his shooting
stories.body: The conservative activist was speaking to a crowd of thousands on the university campus when he was shot and killed by a gunman positioned on a roof.

stories.title: Colombia and Brazil deadliest countries for environmental activists, report says
stories.body: The two countries accounted for 52% of killings of environmental activists in 2025, according to Global Witness.

stories.title: US limits visas for South African officials over alleged anti-white discrimination
stories.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio says South Africa has not addressed US concerns over racial inequality.

stories.title: US accuses Russia of trying to kill Ukrainian allies overseas
stories.body: The FBI says five men "conspired to intimidate, threaten, or murder people on US soil and around the world".

stories.title: Philippines' Duterte seen in person at International Criminal Court for first time
stories.body: He is due to be tried for crimes against humanity over thousands of deaths linked to his war on drugs.

stories.title: Legendary Nigerian actor Olu Jacobs dies aged 84
stories.body: Olu Jacobs was one of Nigeria's most recognised actors, whose career spanned several decades.

stories.title: Tall athletes can't stretch their legs in container beds at Asian Games, official says
stories.body: South Korea's delegation slams the wooden containers housing its athletes at the Asian Games in Nagoya city.

stories.title: Lost on Mount Fuji off-season? You'll have to pay for your rescue
stories.body: The fee will be imposed on those who get lost on Japan's most famous mountain during the off-peak seasons.

stories.title: Why Trump is all-in on AI despite the warnings
stories.body: The US president has pushed the issue to the forefront of American politics - even at the risk of losing supporters.

stories.title: Carney's new love-in with EU has everything to do with Trump
stories.body: The Canadian PM is in Strasbourg this week seeking a "unique alliance" - and there is one clear catalyst.

🟡 **Mood: Cautious**  
Today's signals reflect a cautiously optimistic structural pattern, with notable developments in governance and geopolitical dynamics tempered by contested implications and underlying uncertainty.

**1. Structural Significance of Top Signals**  
The appearance of former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte at the International Criminal Court (ICC) marks a pivotal moment in global accountability mechanisms. This signal, categorized as a "convergent priority," underscores the ICC's growing assertiveness in pursuing high-profile cases, which could set a precedent for other leaders facing allegations of human rights violations. The signal's high knowledge and expression orientation suggest that this event may catalyze broader discourse on international justice systems, though its survival-focused cluster remains weaker, indicating limited immediate impact on global stability.

The U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates for the first time in three years signals a shift in monetary policy aimed at curbing inflation. While the move is categorized as "background noise," its achievement-oriented and stability-seeking clusters highlight its structural importance in recalibrating economic trajectories. However, this action introduces contested implications for global markets, particularly in emerging economies that may face ripple effects from tightened liquidity conditions.

**2. Contested Signals and Diverging Implications**  
The signal surrounding Donald Trump's embrace of AI, despite widespread warnings, presents a contested narrative. While the priority score and achievement orientation suggest alignment with technological advancement, the survival-focused cluster reveals underlying concerns about governance and ethical oversight. This divergence reflects broader tensions between innovation and regulation, with implications for both domestic policy and international AI governance frameworks.

Similarly, the EU's proposal to grant Canada "associate member" status is structurally significant but contested. Its achievement-oriented cluster signals alignment with long-term strategic partnerships, yet its expression-oriented bottom cluster suggests skepticism about the practical feasibility of such an arrangement. This contestedness may reflect broader uncertainties within the EU's geopolitical calculus, particularly as it navigates post-Brexit dynamics and transatlantic relations.

**3. Long-Term Trajectories**  
The ICC's assertiveness in pursuing Duterte could signal a longer-term trend toward strengthening international legal frameworks, particularly in regions with fragile governance structures. Meanwhile, the U.S. interest rate hike may mark the beginning of a sustained tightening cycle, with implications for global economic stability and capital flows. The EU's outreach to Canada hints at evolving transnational alliances, potentially reshaping the geopolitical landscape as traditional blocs adapt to new realities.

**4. What to Watch Next**  
- **ICC proceedings against Duterte:** Monitor for potential ripple effects on other leaders facing international scrutiny and the broader legitimacy of the ICC.  
- **U.S. monetary policy:** Watch for market reactions, especially in emerging economies, and any signals of further rate hikes.  
- **AI governance:** Track developments in regulatory frameworks and international collaboration, particularly in response to Trump's positioning.  
- **EU-Canada partnership:** Observe whether this proposal gains traction and its impact on EU external relations.  

Today's signals reflect a cautious optimism tempered by contested narratives and structural uncertainties. The interplay between governance, economic recalibration, and technological advancement will be critical to shaping near-term trajectories.
